title: Integration-notification prototype (s7): durable, idempotent INTEGRATION_READY notice
objective: Cut integration latency: when a task enters INTEGRATION_READY a durable notice reaches the integrator once, and the queue is visible.
problem: Sidecar in the RSO lane that READS workgraph task state and comms. workgraph/ (Achilles) and comms/ are NOT edited; if a hook inside workgraph.transition is the right design, write it up as a routed proposal to Achilles and still ship the sidecar. Behaviour: (1) `python -m rso.scale.notify scan` finds INTEGRATION_READY tasks for a coordinator's campaigns; (2) emits ONE comms notice per (task_id, attempt / branch head sha), an idempotency key recorded durably (committed or DB-visible, not a local temp file), so a retry or a second scanner never duplicates; (3) `queue` prints the pending integration queue with age; (4) records the disposition when the task later becomes INTEGRATED / CLOSED or is sent back. It never merges, never changes task state, never bypasses tests. A wake for the coordinator may be a documented command (e.g. a one-shot headless launch); install no OS scheduler task.
non_goals: No automatic merge or state change
No edit in another seat's lane
evidence_required: tests: a repeated scan or retry emits one notice; a new attempt sha emits a new one; disposition recorded; no write to workgraph state
a live demonstration against C-016's own packets, with the comms ids
a short README with the wake command

acceptance.condition: all evidence_required items; committed with source references
